sections.h2: Augusta County and its two cities
sections.html:
Augusta County sits in the Shenandoah Valley on the western side of Virginia. The 2020 census counted 77,487 residents, and most of them live in unincorporated communities such as Stuarts Draft, Fishersville and Verona rather than in a town. Craigsville and Grottoes are the two towns.

The county completely surrounds the independent cities of Staunton and Waynesboro, but those cities are separate localities. A house with a Staunton or Waynesboro mailing address may be taxed by the city, while a house just outside the line is taxed by Augusta County. The community name on a mailing label does not decide who bills you. The parcel's location does, so check the county's online assessment records or call the offices before you assume.

Sellers in Stuarts Draft, Fishersville, Verona, Weyers Cave, Crimora or Churchville all deal with the same county offices. Buyers coming from Staunton or Waynesboro often assume the rates and billing match their old city, and they do not, so expect questions about the county bill during negotiation.

Augusta splits the annual bill into two equal halves. A due date that lands on a weekend slides to the Monday after, and owners who prefer one payment can pay everything in June. The county's e-Treasurer site lets you look up and pay a bill online.

InstallmentDue dateLate charge
First halfJune 510 percent penalty, plus 10 percent yearly interest
Second halfDecember 510 percent penalty, plus 10 percent yearly interest

The Board of Supervisors set the 2024 rate at $0.52 per $100 of assessed value, and the Real Estate Assessor's Office values every parcel as of January 1. The penalty applies to the unpaid balance. Interest does not run on the state's share of personal property tax.

Taxpayers are expected to know the due dates. If no bill arrives, contact the taxing office before the date to arrange payment.

sections.h2: When the late charge is waived
sections.html:
The county does not accept these as reasons: you did not know the due date, no bill came, the bill went to a wrong address, the bill was wrong, or a staff member gave bad information. A waiver is possible only in narrower cases:

  • A medically determinable physical or mental impairment on the due date, with payment made within 30 days.
  • The Commissioner of Revenue abates the tax or certifies a clerical error by that office.
  • The late payment was caused solely by the Treasurer or the Commissioner of Revenue.

If you cannot pay the whole amount, ask the Treasurer's Office about a payment plan at (540) 245-5660 or treasurer@co.augusta.va.us. The plan leaves the penalty in place, and interest continues on whatever is still owed.

Augusta reassesses on a five-year cycle. The 2024 reassessment started in September 2022, with notices mailed in February 2024. The county hired Wampler-Eanes Appraisal Group, which split the county into about 96 neighborhoods and visited accessible properties to check records and update property cards and photos.

The county's analysis of 2023 residential sales covered 680 sales. Values rose a median of 58.3 percent over the old assessment, with an average of 60.9 percent. The biggest median increases were in Beverly Manor (69.5 percent) and North River (68.8 percent). The smallest were in Craigsville (33.7 percent, from only three sales) and Wayne (50.9 percent).

The jump has a reason. Virginia's sales ratio study flags a locality whose assessments fall below 70 percent of fair market value in a general reassessment year, and Augusta's ratios had slid to 89.75 percent in 2019, 83.73 percent in 2020 and 71.7 percent in 2021. If your own value climbed sharply, remember it is the county's estimate, not a sale price. A buyer will still pay what the market supports.

The county lays out three stages: an informal hearing with the assessor, the Board of Equalization, and finally Circuit Court. The informal stage could be handled by Zoom, phone, email, mail or a visit.

  • Reasons people raise: a value that seems too high or too low, market value disparities, changes in condition, comparable sales and clerical errors.
  • Deadlines are printed on your notice, so read it as soon as it arrives.

Under Virginia Code section 58.1-3381 the board can increase, decrease or affirm an assessment, and the owner must be notified before an increase. In court, section 58.1-3984 treats the assessor's value as correct, and the owner has to rebut it by a preponderance of the evidence.

For the informal hearing, bring photos, repair estimates and recent comparable sales. Defects the assessor cannot see from the street are worth pointing out right away.

A sale does not erase a tax debt. Virginia Code section 58.1-3340 attaches a first-position lien to real estate, so the closing agent settles the balance from your proceeds. The contract says how the current year is divided.

Late charges have a state ceiling in section 58.1-3916: 10 percent of the overdue tax or $10, whichever is more, plus interest up to 10 percent a year. Augusta charges right up to that ceiling.

At closing, expect two deed taxes. The grantor tax is 50 cents for each $500 (section 58.1-802) and lands on the seller by default. The recordation tax is 25 cents per $100 (section 58.1-801).

  1. Ask the Treasurer for a payoff figure before closing.
  2. Pay or schedule any open installment.
  3. Keep the receipt for your title company.

sections.h2: What to have ready before you sell
sections.html:
Pull together your assessment notice and your recent tax bills so you can see which installments are paid. Search the parcel in the county's online records to confirm that Augusta County, and not Staunton or Waynesboro, taxes it. The Treasurer's Office at (540) 245-5660 can give you a payoff figure, and the assessor's office can answer questions about a value that looks wrong.

Already on a payment plan? Tell your closing agent early, because the lien must be cleared before a buyer gets clean title. A planned contest of the 2024 value should wait for a folder of photos and comparable sales.

On closing day the title company takes the open balance and your share of the current year out of the proceeds, records the deed, and sends you the rest. Nothing about a Shenandoah Valley sale changes that order, and the whole process can take place without you visiting the Treasurer's office in person if your closing agent handles the payoff.

Owners who inherited a house, moved away, or got a reassessment notice they did not expect sometimes want a shorter route than listing. We buy houses as they are and give a written cash offer, so an open tax balance or deferred repairs are things we can work through with you. A cash sale skips showings, buyer financing and repair negotiations. Call or text the address and we will go from there.

faqs.q: Are Staunton and Waynesboro part of Augusta County?
faqs.a: No. They are independent cities that Augusta County surrounds. A house inside either city is generally handled by the city, so check which office bills you.

faqs.q: When are Augusta County property taxes due?
faqs.a: June 5 and December 5. A due date on a weekend moves to the following Monday.

faqs.q: What is the late penalty in Augusta County?
faqs.a: 10 percent of the unpaid balance, plus 10 percent annual interest. A payment plan does not remove either charge.

faqs.q: Who do I contact about a payment plan?
faqs.a: The Treasurer's Office at (540) 245-5660 or treasurer@co.augusta.va.us.

faqs.q: How many years between Augusta County reassessments?
faqs.a: Five. The latest reassessment took effect in 2024.
